column1: # Where the JDK's locale data makes a placeholder resolve to different text than on a Mac.
# JvmDateRenderer does not reproduce byte for byte. Every row is a difference in CLDR data
# between macOS 27.2 (which emitted the vectors) and the JDK 17 that recorded this list; none
# is a difference in the resolver. SwiftPlaceholderVectorsTest fails for any difference that is
# not listed here, and for any row here that no longer differs. On Android the app formats
# with the device's ICU (android.icu), whose data is close to the Mac's, so these rows say
# what the :core fallback renderer prints, not what users see.
#   narrow-no-break-space  CLDR 42 put U+202F before AM/PM in English; older data has a space.
#   medium-style-pattern   The medium style itself differs: "{date} at {time}" / "{date} à {time}"
#                          against "{date}, {time}"; sr-Latn "d. M. y." against "dd.MM.y."; the
#                          commas of the ar-SA Hijri date.
#   name-spelling          Thai AM/PM: "AM"/"PM" on the Mac, the Thai words in the JDK.
#   day-period             B ("at night", "in the morning"): the JDK prints the AM/PM marker.
#   zone-name              z: the Mac prints "GMT", "GMT+1", "UTC+1"; the JDK "UTC", "CET".
#   calendar-not-in-jdk    fa-IR defaults to the Persian calendar, which the JDK does not have.
# file<TAB>case<TAB>class<TAB>template<TAB>Swift on macOS<TAB>JvmDateRenderer on JDK 17<TAB>the same three as UTF-8 hex
